title: Compatible Brown transformations on a telescope
statement: Let C be triangulated [def-weil-triangulated-category] with morphism universe v and Type v indexed coproducts. Let X : ℕ → C, let H : C opposite → AddCommGrpCat v be homological [def-sp-homological-functor] and preserve Type v indexed products, and let β_j : Hom_C(-,X_j) → H be natural transformations compatible with every successor transition. There exist G, maps ι_j : X_j → G, and α : Hom_C(-,G) → H. Successor transition followed by ι_(j+1) is ι_j; Hom(-,ι_j) followed by α is β_j. For every compact K [def-pc-compact-object], integer n and f : K[n] → G, there are j and g : K[n] → X_j with g followed by ι_j equal to f. No surjectivity or kernel-killing assumption on β is made, and no bijectivity of α is asserted.

proof.text: Compactness is preserved by integer shifts. Take the additive adjunction between shift by n and by -n. Its homAddEquiv identifies the summand Hom groups. The inverse shift preserves coproducts, so its sigmaComparison is invertible. Postcomposition with its inverse identifies the total Hom groups. DirectSum.congrAddEquiv gives the sum comparison; equality on each summand follows from adjunction naturality and map_ι_comp_inv_sigmaComparison. Thus the new compactness comparison is conjugate by additive equivalences to the old bijective comparison.

Form A as the coproduct of X_j indexed by ULift ℕ and let d be the coproduct-desc transition shift. Complete 1-d to a distinguished triangle A → A → G → A[1]. Put ι_j equal to the inclusion followed by its second arrow. Restrict the zero composite (1-d) followed by that arrow to each summand and expand the difference to obtain successor compatibility.

Reuse BrownStageSequence's private elementTransformation, stage_elementTransformation_value, stage_coproduct_element and stage_coproduct_element_zero through proof-only import all; brownStageSequence itself is not applied. The recovery formula follows from naturality evaluated at the identity. The coproduct element and zero criterion follow from the limiting fan universal property after applying H and the forgetful functor to types. Evaluate β_j at the identity to obtain a_j. Their successor compatibility follows by naturality and the given equality of transformations. Product preservation assembles a_j into x in H(A). The value H(1-d)(x) has zero restriction to each summand by compatibility, hence is zero by the limiting fan universal property. Homological exactness lifts x to y in H(G). The explicitly constructed transformation f ↦ H(f)(y) is α; functoriality, the summand values of x and naturality recover β_j on restriction along ι_j.

Apply compact_hom_hocolim to K[n], compact by the first step, and the constructed telescope triangle. Its comparison is surjective. Every element of a colimit of types is represented at some stage (Types.jointly_surjective'). Its specified value under the comparison gives exactly the required factorization through ι_j.

lean.statement:
theorem brownTelescopeAssembly (X : ℕ ⥤ C)
    (H : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{v}) [H.IsHomological]
    (hH : ∀ (J : Type v), PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete J) H)
    (β : ∀ j : ℕ, preadditiveYoneda.obj (X.obj j) ⟶ H)
    (hβ : ∀ j : ℕ,
      preadditiveYoneda.map (X.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ j))) ≫ β (j + 1) = β j) :
    ∃ (G : C) (ι : ∀ j : ℕ, X.obj j ⟶ G) (α : preadditiveYoneda.obj G ⟶ H),
      (∀ j : ℕ, X.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ j)) ≫ ι (j + 1) = ι j) ∧
      (∀ j : ℕ, preadditiveYoneda.map (ι j) ≫ α = β j) ∧
      (∀ (K : C), IsCompactObject K → ∀ (n : ℤ) (f : K⟦n⟧ ⟶ G),
        ∃ (j : ℕ) (g : K⟦n⟧ ⟶ X.obj j), g ≫ ι j = f)
